PockPock Agent 0.2.16 adds **PockPock Code**, a coding agent for your terminal that runs on your local models. Plan in steps can now hand steps that need a real shell, installs or a browser to OpenClaw, and still checks each one. Word and PDF documents are fixed: a resume in Word and PDF now produces both files.

## Download

| Your computer | Download |
|---|---|
| Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) | [PockPock-Agent-Setup.exe](https://github.com/PockPock9/PockPockAgent/releases/latest/download/PockPock-Agent-Setup.exe) |
| Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or newer) | [PockPock-Agent-mac-arm64.dmg](https://github.com/PockPock9/PockPockAgent/releases/latest/download/PockPock-Agent-mac-arm64.dmg) |
| Mac with an Intel processor | [PockPock-Agent-mac-x64.dmg](https://github.com/PockPock9/PockPockAgent/releases/latest/download/PockPock-Agent-mac-x64.dmg) |

**Already using 0.2.15 on Windows?** PockPock updates itself: press **Restart to update** when it appears, or check in **Settings → Updates**. Your chats, settings, models and caches are kept. Before the services start, this update also installs two new Python packages, one for PDF files and one for the terminal. On a Mac, download and install it once, the same way as the first time.

**New to PockPock?** Open the downloaded file, then press **Set up PockPock**; setup installs everything else. Windows may show **"Windows protected your PC"** because PockPock is not code-signed yet: press **More info**, then **Run anyway**. On a Mac, see the [installation guide](https://github.com/PockPock9/PockPockAgent/wiki/Installation).

## What's new since 0.2.15

### PockPock Code in the terminal

Open a terminal in a project folder and type `pockpock-code`. It reads the code, answers with file and line references, edits files, runs your tests and fixes what fails, all on your local models.

```
pockpock-code                          # a session in the current folder
pockpock-code "fix the failing test"   # start with a request
pockpock-code -p "explain src/app.py"  # answer once and exit
```

- **Your control.** It asks before running commands. Add `--mode suggest` to approve edits too, or `--mode full-auto` to approve nothing. `/undo` restores the files the last request changed.
- **Three engines.** By default (`--engine code`) it does the work itself with a small, fast prompt. `--engine pockpock` hands the request to PockPock Agent (add `--planner qwen3.8:27b` for Plan in steps), `--engine openclaw` hands it to OpenClaw, and `--engine auto` chooses per request. In every engine you see the same tool lines and approvals.
- **Install.** PockPock adds the command after setup. Open a new terminal the first time.

### OpenClaw does the steps that need a real computer

In **Plan in steps**, a step that has to run or build a project (`npm install`, `npm test`, `pytest`), install a tool, or use a browser or app can now be handed to OpenClaw. PockPock still writes the plan and checks every step itself. If OpenClaw's step doesn't pass its check, PockPock sends it back with what was missing. OpenClaw uses the same model as the run, so nothing extra is loaded, and its actions and approval cards appear in the run.

Tested with `qwen3.5:9b`:
- a Node.js project whose tests then ran: 44 s;
- a script run with its output saved: 36 s;
- a bug fixed and its tests re-run: 96 s.

### Word, PDF, Excel and slides

- **PDF files.** "A resume in Word and PDF" could never produce the PDF before. Now it can.
- **Real Word formatting.** Word documents get real headings, bullet lists and bold, in a single column that applicant tracking systems (ATS) read reliably. Before, they showed "## Experience" as plain text.
- **The format you ask for.** "A PDF report" no longer comes out as a Word file.
- **Numbers in Excel.** Spreadsheet numbers are real numbers, so totals work.
- **Slides.** Each heading starts its own slide.

### Fewer failed plans

- **Empty folders.** In an empty folder, plans no longer try to read documents that don't exist.
- **Small planner mistakes.** A stray field in a step's check no longer rejects the whole plan.
- **Tests that should fail first.** A step that runs tests to see them fail is no longer expected to pass them.
- **PowerShell output.** Files saved by PowerShell (UTF-16) are read correctly by the checks.

## Good to know

- Both pull requests passed the full check suite (backend tests, and the desktop typecheck and build, on Ubuntu, Windows and macOS).
- Not tested yet: PockPock Code on macOS, and very long terminal sessions. A full re-run of 100 everyday tasks on this version is in progress.
